hook.line: When Tomás isn't sure the council will listen, he can't say *they will*. He says he doubts it, and Spanish changes the verb to show it.
hook.es: No estoy seguro de que me escuchen.
hook.en: I'm not sure they'll listen to me.

rule:
*Estoy seguro de que* means you're certain, so the verb after it is the plain one: *Estoy seguro de que viene.*

Put *no* in front and you aren't sure, so the verb after *de que* takes the *-e* or *-a* form: *No estoy seguro de que venga.*

Soften with *del todo* (entirely) or swap in *convencido*. Both stay the same: *No estoy del todo seguro de que...*

*Seguro* ends in *-o* for a man and *-a* for a woman. Never drop the *de* before *que*.

For something already finished, use *haya* plus the *-ado* or *-ido* word: *hayan oído*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the subjunctive after a negated certainty.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *viene* or *venga*, then type the whole sentence: No estoy seguro de que ___. (I'm not sure he's coming, a man speaking.)
yourTurn.answer: No estoy seguro de que venga.
yourTurn.why: Not sure means the *-a* form after *de que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *viene* or *venga*, then type the whole sentence: Estoy seguro de que ___. (I'm sure he's coming, a man speaking.)
yourTurn.why: Certain means the plain verb, with no change.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I'm not sure he's coming. (a woman speaking)
yourTurn.answer: No estoy segura de que venga.
yourTurn.why: A woman speaking gets *segura*, and doubt gets *venga*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I'm not convinced it's the best option. (a man speaking)
yourTurn.answer: No estoy convencido de que sea la mejor opción.
yourTurn.why: *Convencido* works like *seguro*, with the *-e* or *-a* form after *de que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I'm not sure the council will listen. (a man speaking)
yourTurn.answer: No estoy seguro de que el concejo escuche.
yourTurn.why: Doubt after *de que* means the *-e* form of *escuchar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: Estoy seguro de que viene. (a man speaking)
yourTurn.answer: No estoy seguro de que venga.
yourTurn.why: Add *no*, then the verb changes to the *-a* form.

yourTurn.prompt: Soften it: No estoy seguro de que venga. (a man speaking, add *entirely*)
yourTurn.answer: No estoy del todo seguro de que venga.
yourTurn.why: *Del todo* goes right before *seguro* and makes it gentler.
